lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: Come in, sit. You've been solid since the swearing-in, {playerFirst}, which is why I'd like this to be a short conversation.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: The coffee's terrible, but it's hot. I won't keep you long. It's about {bill}.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: Close the door, would you. I'd like to know where you stand on {bill} before I read about it in a {playerRiding} weekly.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: Your name came up at the morning count. Nobody's sure what you'll do on {bill}. That includes me.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: Sit down. I've had three calls about your remarks on {bill}, and none of them were from people who like you.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: You've missed two votes we needed this month. Before we get to {bill}, I'd like to hear why.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: I'll be honest: the count on {bill} is tighter than I'd like, and you're one of the names I can't mark yet.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: {bill} isn't popular in {playerRiding}. I know. {leader} needs it through second reading, and I need every hand we've got.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: Vote with us on this one and the office will remember it. We have long memories here, and they work both ways.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: I don't need you to love {bill}. I need you in your seat, on your feet, when the yeas are called.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: Vote against {bill} and committee assignments get very hard to come by. That's not a threat. It's just how the office works.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: If four of ours walk on {bill}, we lose it. In a minority, losing it isn't an embarrassment. It's an election.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: Tell me what it would take. I'm not promising anything, I'm asking. The count is that close.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: So I can mark you down as a yea? I'd like to give {leader} some good news before the bells.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: Whatever you choose, tell me first. That's the one rule I really care about.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: I need an answer I can write on the board. Yea, nay, or a very good reason to be in the washroom.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: Last chance to make this easy. What do I tell {leader} about you?

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: The bells could ring tomorrow. Whatever you decide, don't let me find out from the Clerk.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Thanks for making time. I know you've got the whole caucus to chase this week.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: You want to know how I'm voting on {bill}. Ask me plainly.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Before I say anything, what are you hearing about {bill} in caucus?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: If this is about {bill}, my riding's against it, and they're the ones who hired me.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Is this about the committee schedule? I've been meaning to ask about that.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I know I've been hard to reach. That's on me. What do you need?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I want to help you. I also have to face the people at the legion hall on Friday.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: If I vote yea, {playerRiding} needs something to show for it. What can the office do?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Walk me through why {leader} won't move on {bill}. I'd like to understand it.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Leaning on me won't move me. My riding will. Give me something I can sell at home.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I haven't finished reading the amendments. Can we come back to this after the weekend?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Fine. I don't like {bill}, but I won't be the one who sinks it.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Whatever I decide, you'll hear it from me before anyone else. You have my word.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Mark me yea if the office backs my riding's infrastructure application. Otherwise, I'm undecided.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Show me the latest count first. Then I'll give you a straight answer.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Put me down as a nay. I'd rather explain it to you than to {playerRiding}.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Mark me as leaning. I'll know more after I talk to my riding office.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Put me down as a yea. I'll be in my seat.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: {name}, {riding}. We were sworn in the same morning. I sat two chairs down and dropped my pen during the oath.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Mind if I sit? Everyone keeps telling me to get to know the cohort, and you're the only one who answers your door.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I'm {name}. I like to know who I'm sitting beside before the whip decides it for me.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I've heard a few things about you. Thought I'd come and find out which of them are true.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Fair warning, I've had a day. The whip's office moved my QP slot and nobody told me why. I'm {name}, {riding}.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Sorry to drop in like this. I'm {name}. I still get lost in the tunnels between here and the committee rooms.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I'm {name}. Is it always like this, or did we just get elected in a bad month?

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I'm mostly on the {interest} file. If you care about it too, we should be talking before the committee does.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: A few of us in {clique} have dinner on Wednesdays. Nothing formal. You'd be welcome.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: What brought you to the House? Everyone has a reason, and it's usually not the one in their householder.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Here's my problem: they whip us like a herd and then wonder why nobody in {riding} trusts politicians.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: My margin in {riding} was a few hundred votes. I can't afford to get on the wrong side of anyone this year.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Good. My door's down the hall, the one with the crooked nameplate. Use it whenever.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Let's do this again after the next vote. We'll have more to complain about by then.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: All right. I'll take you at your word until I have a reason not to.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Well. At least you listened, which is more than I can say for the whip's office.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Thanks. It helps to know someone else here is also making it up as they go.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Come in, sit down. I've been hoping someone from the cohort would knock.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Good to meet you. What's on your mind?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Tell me about {riding}. What's it like out there?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Glad you came by. I'll need allies here, and I remember who showed up early.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'm still figuring out which hallway is which. Have you found decent coffee yet?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I should have come to you first. Sorry, the first weeks have been a blur.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: My family thinks I've moved to the moon. How is yours taking it?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: So what do you want out of this Parliament? Committee, cabinet, or just re-election?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: That sounds like it's been weighing on you. Go on.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: If we're going to work together, I need to know you won't fold the first time the whip calls.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Let's not get into all that yet. Tell me who the good staffers are.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: You're right. I came in thinking I knew how this place worked. I didn't.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: My door's open any evening. Bring the bad coffee.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Let's trade numbers. If something's coming on {interest}, I'd like a call.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'll remember what you said. Come back any time you need to think out loud.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'll hold you to that. In this place, people remember who kept their word.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Let's see how the next few weeks go before we make any plans.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'll follow your lead on {interest}. You know the file better than I do.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Got a minute? I've got a small ask, and I promise it really is small.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: {playerFirst}. Just the person. Do you have a pen and five minutes?

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I'll be direct, because I don't like owing people. I need something, and you might be able to give it.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I've been turned down twice today. I'm hoping you'll be the exception.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I hate doing this, but I'm out of options and the deadline's tomorrow morning.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Sorry, is now bad? It's about my riding, and it can't really wait.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I've got a private member's motion on {interest}. It needs a second name, and yours would look good on it.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Your Member's Statement on Thursday. If you could spare fifteen seconds for {riding}, I'd owe you one.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: There's a seat opening on the {interest} committee. A word from you to {mentor} wouldn't hurt me.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: When {bill} gets to committee, I'm moving an amendment. I'd like your vote on it, and your name if you'll give it.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: The mill in {riding} is closing and nobody on our side has said a word in the House. I want your QP slot.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: My riding thinks I've forgotten them. If you'd co-sponsor my petition on {interest}, they'd see someone's listening.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: So, can I put your name down? I'll make sure you get the credit.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Think it over. Either way, I appreciate you hearing me out.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I don't need an answer tonight. But I'll know what it means if I don't get one.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Yes or no. I've had enough maybes this week to last me the Parliament.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: If you can do it, I won't forget it. And if you can't, I'd rather know now.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Of course. Sit down, you look like you've been running all day.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: What do you need?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Go ahead, I'm listening. Start from the beginning.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Before you ask, remember I'm a rookie too. Favours here aren't free.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'm swamped tonight. Can this wait for the weekend?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: If I can help, I will. What is it?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I know what {riding} means to you. I'd want someone to do the same for mine.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I can do that. What do I get in return?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Why me, and why now? Help me understand what's riding on it.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: The last favour like that ended up on the whip's desk. Has the office cleared this?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Let me check with my office. I'm not sure what I've already committed to.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: All right. It's not much to give, and you'd do the same for me.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Put my name down. {riding} deserves someone in its corner.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Done. And when I need a second name on something, I'm coming to you.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Let me sleep on it. Is there anything else I should know first?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'll do it once. Don't make a habit of asking.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'll see what I can do. No promises.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: You've got it. Consider it done.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Shut the door. You'll want to hear this before Wednesday's caucus.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I shouldn't be telling you this, so you didn't hear it from me.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: You won't believe what {other} said about our cohort in the lobby this afternoon.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Have you heard anything? People are whispering, and I can't tell whether it's about me.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: {other} has had lunch with the whip twice this week. Nobody gets two lunches unless something's being arranged.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Word is the whip's office is drawing up a list of soft votes. Some of the cohort are on it. I don't know who.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: {other} went over our heads to the leader's office about money for {otherRiding}. Now the whole envelope is frozen.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: There's talk of a committee shuffle, and {clique} wants its own people protected. I'm not sure I count.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Anyway. You didn't get it from me, and I'll expect the same courtesy one day.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Keep it to yourself for a week. If it's true, you'll know soon enough.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Someone needs to say something to {other}. I'm just saying it shouldn't have to be me.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: If you hear anything about me, will you tell me? I'd do the same for you.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Come in. You look like you need to sit down.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: What happened?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'm listening. Take your time.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: If this is going to land either of us in trouble, tell me now.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I try to stay out of lobby chatter, honestly.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: You're right, I've been out of the loop. Catch me up.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: That's rough. Are you all right?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Who else knows? And how did you hear?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Interesting. What do you make of it?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: You can't sit on that. If {other} is freelancing, the whip should know.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Could be nothing. Half of what goes around this place is wrong by Thursday.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: You're probably right. I hadn't seen it, but it fits.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Thanks for trusting me with it. That means something.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Keep me posted. If it touches my riding, I need to know the same day.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'll keep my ears open and tell you what I hear.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Next time, come to me before you go to anyone else. Agreed?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Let's see how it plays out. No point getting ahead of ourselves.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: All right, I'll keep it quiet. You have my word.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Got a minute? A few of us have been talking about {bill}, and your name came up. In a good way.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: This conversation isn't happening, all right? I'm here about {bill}.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I'm tired of being told to stand up for things that gut my riding. You've read what's in {bill}.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I need to ask you something, and I need you not to repeat it to the whip's office.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: We've got five, maybe six who'll vote against {bill} at second reading. With you, the whip has to come to the table.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: We're not trying to bring the government down. We want an amendment on {interest}, and a nay is our only leverage.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: {bill} hits {riding} and {playerRiding} the same way. If we don't stand together, they'll pick us off one at a time.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: If I go alone, I'm finished. If enough of us go, it's a message. I'm trying to find out which it'll be.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Can I count you in? We're meeting in my office after QP tomorrow.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Think about it. But if the whip hears about this before the vote, I'll know where it came from.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: So are you with us, or are you going to stand up and clap while they gut our ridings?

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I need to know by the weekend. If it's no, I'd rather pull out than go down alone.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Come in. Whatever this is, you can talk freely here.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Who else is involved?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Go on. I've had my own doubts about {bill}.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Careful. The whip's office keeps track of which doors people walk through.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I haven't really looked at {bill} closely yet.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I've been waiting for someone to say it out loud.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I hear you. I've got people at home who'd be hit just as hard.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: What's the ask, exactly? An amendment, a delay, or a defeat?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: How many have you really got? And who's wavering?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: If this fails, you take the rest of us down with you. Have you thought that through?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'd want to see the committee report before I decide anything.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: You're right. Someone has to make them listen on {bill}.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Whatever I decide, I'll tell you to your face first.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'm in if the ask is an amendment. I won't vote to bring the government down.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Let me think on it. Tell me how the others land.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'm not in, and I'd think hard before you go any further.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Let's talk after the weekend. I need to hear from my riding first.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Count me in. My riding would never forgive me otherwise.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Mind if I sit? I've been in this building a long time, and I still like the view from a backbencher's window.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I've been hearing things about you. Not all bad. I thought we should talk before the whip does.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I put my name next to yours when you got here, {playerFirst}. Why am I hearing about you from the whip's office?

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I won't stay long. Something's shifting in caucus, and I'd rather you were ready for it.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Here's what nobody tells rookies: the whip cares less about how you vote than whether you told the office first.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Your riding elected you, but caucus decides whether you get anything for them. Keep both happy, or choose which to lose.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: You can't make speeches in the lobby and expect the leader's office not to hear. This building has more ears than doors.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: If you're thinking of crossing the whip on {bill}, I need to know. My name is tied to yours whether we like it or not.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Go home on Friday, eat at the diner, let people yell at you. That's worth more than any committee seat.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: You'll make your own choices. Just make sure they're choices and not accidents.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I'm not done with you. But I'd like you to make it a little easier for me to keep saying that.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Whatever happens this week, keep your head down and your phone on.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Always. Sit down, I was hoping you'd come by.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: What's on your mind?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'm glad you came. What are you hearing?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: If this is about my vote, I've already made up my mind.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Is this about the dinner on Thursday? I'll be there, I promise.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I know, I should have come to you first. I'm sorry.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I don't know what I'd do without you in this place. Honestly.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Tell me straight: what does the whip think of me right now?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: How did you handle it, your first Parliament?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: With respect, your seat is safe. I won mine by a few hundred votes.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: That's fair. Can we talk about committees instead?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: You're right. I'll be more careful, starting now.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Thank you. I mean it. I'll try to make you look good.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Could you put in a word for me on the {interest} committee?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'll think about all of it. Anything else I should be watching?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'll listen, but I won't vote against my riding just to keep the office happy.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Let's see how the week shakes out.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Understood. I'll follow your lead on this one.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I'd rather say this to your face than to anyone else, so here I am.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: We need to talk about something you said. I'll give you the chance to explain first.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Do you know what you've done? I spent the afternoon on the phone with my riding association because of you.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I'm not here to fight. But something's been bothering me, and it's getting worse, not better.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Your Member's Statement on the port expansion left {riding} out. People at home noticed. So did I.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: You voted with the opposition on my committee amendment. I found out from a reporter.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: You told {other} what I said about {bill}. In confidence. Now the whip's office knows.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: {other} has been telling people I'm a soft vote, and they say you're the one who started it.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I'm not asking for much. Just fix it, and we'll leave it there.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I'll take your word for it this time. There won't be a second time.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I want it put right, publicly. Otherwise don't expect me to stand up for you in caucus.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I just need to know I can trust you. Can I?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'm glad you came to me. Sit down, let's sort it out.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: All right. What did I do?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Go ahead. I won't interrupt.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Before you start, remember I've backed you more than once.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Is this really the time? The bells could ring any minute.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: If I've caused you trouble, I'm sorry. Tell me what happened.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I never meant for it to land on you like that. I'm sorry you've had a rough week.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: What would put it right? Tell me, and I'll see if I can do it.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I didn't know it hit you that hard. What are people saying?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I stand by it. I'd do it again, and so would you in my seat.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I think there's been a misunderstanding. Let's not blow this out of proportion.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: You're right. I should have warned you first. That was a mistake.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: We're in this together for the next four years. I'd rather we were friends.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'll mention {riding} in my next statement. Does that square us?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Thanks for telling me straight. Is there anything else I should know?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'll fix this, but don't threaten me in caucus. That won't help either of us.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Let's give it a few days and see how it looks then.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'll set it right, publicly. You have my word.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I brought two coffees. One's for you. The other's in case you've got bad news.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I won't take long. I'd just like to hear a few things from you before I hear them in the lobby.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Is your door shut? Never mind. Nobody shuts anything in this building, which is half the trouble.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: The members who last here aren't the clever ones. They're the ones who return calls by six, from their own phone.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Pick three people in this caucus you'll never surprise. The whip, whoever sits next to you in the lobby, and me, ideally.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: When caucus gets like this, people remember who was in the room and who was talking to the press gallery. Be in the room.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Right, I've kept you from your mail long enough. Read the letters from home first. The rest can wait.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: You don't have to take my advice. Just don't make me find out from someone else that you didn't.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Ring me if anything changes. Anything. In weeks like this I sleep with the phone on the pillow.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Look at you, with a door that closes. I knocked anyway. Old habits.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I won't keep you. I know your evenings belong to the count now.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I'm not here for a favour. I'd like that on the record before you start wondering.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: People have started asking me what you're like. I've been saying 'fair'. I'd like to keep saying it.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Five minutes? The back rows are talking, and they've stopped talking in front of you.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I've come to warn the whip's office about something, which is a strange errand for a backbencher. Bear with me.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Remember the other side of that desk. Everyone you're counting is as frightened as you were in your first month.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Spend your favours on people who'll still be here in ten years, not on whoever's shouting loudest this week.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: The office will change you. That isn't a criticism. Decide now which parts of you it's allowed to have.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Not long ago you were the one being counted. Try to remember how that felt while you're doing the counting.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: There are members who think you keep a list. Whether you do or not, they've started behaving as if you do.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: The whip's office hears everything except the thing that matters. Here's the thing that matters: the back rows are tired.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Go on, then. Your phone's been buzzing the whole time I've been sitting here.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I'm proud of you. Don't repeat that. It'll ruin my reputation for misery.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: You'll do what the office needs. Just leave a little of yourself for the riding.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: If you ever need someone to tell you you're wrong, mine's the door without the brass plate.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Watch the ones who go quiet. The loud ones come round in the end. The quiet ones just don't turn up.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: If the next count goes wrong, come and find me before you go and find the leader.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I read the division list this morning. I'd have preferred to hear it from you.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: About the vote. Breaking the whip once is a conviction. Twice is a habit, and the office files habits differently.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I saw your name on the wrong side. I'm not angry. I want to know you'd do it again, because if you wouldn't, it wasn't worth it.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: You've voted the line every time so far. Good. Now make them notice, which is a different job entirely.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Reliable is a reputation. Make sure it doesn't turn into taken for granted.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Your constituency office rang mine by mistake. I took the message. It wasn't a happy one.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Someone from {playerRiding} called me. They didn't say anything bad, which is how I knew it was bad. Go home this Friday.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Your association president has started saying 'our member' instead of your name. That's how it starts.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: {playerRiding} likes you. Bank it. One day there'll be a vote that costs all of it at once.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: {rival} has been in to see the whip twice this month. I'm not saying go three times. I'm saying you should know.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Don't run against {rival}. Run past them. The whip notices who does the work, not who complains about the other one.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I wasn't sure I'd still be let in without an appointment.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Congratulations on the desk. The first thing they'll test is whether you still answer the phone to people who can't help you.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: The day you got the office, three people asked me if you'd be soft. I said no. Prove me half right.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I came to see how you're taking it. Badly, by the look of the desk.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: So you're back with us. Don't sulk in the lobby. The ones who come back are the ones who were seen taking it well.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: They took the office, not your seat. You know this building better than you did a year ago. Use that.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: The leader's office is asking about you. Not the whip, the leader's office. Bring them good news soon.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I've seen whips replaced for less than the month you're having. Get one clean vote through and the talk stops.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Come in. You're the only person this week who's knocked instead of phoning.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: You don't drop by for nothing. What is it?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Sit. Tell me what the lobby's saying, and leave nothing out.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Before you start: I've thought hard about where I stand, and I'd like that respected.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Is this social? I've got forty letters to sign before the bells.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I've been meaning to come and find you. I should have done it sooner.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: You make it sound almost survivable.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Who should I be talking to that I'm not?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: What would you have done, in my seat?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I didn't come here to be a vote the office can count without asking.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: That's a lot for a Tuesday. Can we come back to it?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: All right. I'll take that to heart.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Same time next week? I'll bring better coffee.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: If something opens up, would you say my name in the right room?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Who else should I be watching?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'll weigh it. But the riding gets the last word, not the office.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Let me sleep on it.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'll do it your way. You haven't steered me wrong yet.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: You never need an appointment. Sit, please.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I've got ten minutes before the count. What's happening?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I was hoping you'd come. Nobody tells me anything straight any more.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: If this is about a member you'd like me to go easy on, I'll hear it. I won't promise.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Is it urgent? The office has me on three things at once.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I've been bad about keeping in touch since the move. I'm sorry.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I still think about my first week, and you telling me where the decent coffee was.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Give me names. Who's tired, and who's tired enough to do something about it?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: What did you see go wrong for the last whip who sat here?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: The office asks a lot of people. I won't apologise for asking it of the office too.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: It looks worse from outside than it is. Mostly.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: You're right. I've been counting heads and forgetting they're people.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Thank you. Truly. Come back whenever, and don't wait for trouble.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: If there's something you want for your riding, tell me now, while I can still get it.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Keep telling me what the back rows say. I can't hear them from in here.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'll keep the office honest. Hold me to that.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: We'll see. The week's barely started.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'll go easier on the back rows. You've earned the right to ask.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: {name}, {riding}. I'm told new members are meant to say hello to the whip's office. So: hello.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I'm {name}. Everyone says you're the one to know if I want to last a whole Parliament.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I'm {name}. They told me to introduce myself to the whip's office and not to say anything I'd regret. I'm trying to do both.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Come in. The office can spare five minutes for a new face.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Welcome. I'll be straight with you: this office remembers who keeps their word. So do I.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Good to meet you. Found your way round yet? The tunnels take about a year.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I should have come to find you. The office has eaten my evenings.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: You're right. I've been here long enough to forget what it's like to be new.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Before you ask: if it goes through this office, it goes in the book.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: Sit, sit. This isn't a summons, it's a conversation. Though I grant you the chair's the same.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: You sit in this office now, {playerFirst}, which makes it stranger that I'm asking. {bill}. Where are you?

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: I keep a board, you've seen it. Your name's in pencil beside {bill}. I'd like to go over it in ink tonight.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: Someone from {playerRiding} rang the leader's office about {bill} this afternoon. They mentioned you by name. So here we are.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: I'll skip the pleasantries. You've been telling people in the lobby you're 'thinking about' {bill}. Think out loud. Here. Now.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: Do you know how many members I've got to see before the bells? Eleven. You're the one I shouldn't have had to.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: Shut the door. I've just come from the leader's office and I need good news, and you're the nearest thing to it I could find.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: I'm going to be straight because there isn't time to be anything else. {bill} is on a knife-edge, and the other side knows it.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: I know the case against {bill}. I've made half of it myself, upstairs. We're past that. It's going to a vote, and I'd like your hand in the air.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: Nobody's asking you to speak for {bill}. Keep your head down, keep your seat warm, and stand when I stand.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: I won't pretend {bill} does anything for {playerRiding}. I'm asking you to remember what the party's done for you, and what it still can.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: Every time one of ours wobbles on {bill}, the other side's whip buys a round. I'm tired of paying for their drinks.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: You think this is about one vote. It isn't. It's about whether I can tell {leader} your word is worth anything.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: I've got a pair I can't use, two members on planes and one in hospital. {bill} comes down to people like you. That isn't flattery.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: Right. Tell me yea and I'll have a quieter night than I deserve.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: Let's finish where we started. {bill}: yea, nay, or tell me now that you don't know, and I'll plan around you.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: I'm writing your name on the board as I leave this room. Tell me what to write beside it.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: I've been patient. I'm told I'm not known for it. Yea or nay on {bill}, and I'll remember which.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: You can walk out of here as a vote or as a problem. I'd prefer the vote. I can manage the problem.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: If it goes wrong on {bill}, they'll ask me who I lost and when I knew. I'd rather not say your name twice.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: Promise me one thing. If you can't do it, don't stand in the lobby pretending you might. I count heads, not hopes.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: Last time you sat in that chair you told me one thing and did another. I'm giving you a second chance to tell me the truth.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: You've never once given me a bad night. I'd like to keep it that way, which is why you're here early.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: I hear {playerRiding} is making your life difficult. I'm about to make it worse, and I'm sorry about that.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: You've been on the other side of this desk. You know what I'm about to ask and why. Don't make me say it the long way.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: The leader's office asked me about you by name this morning. I said you were solid. Help me not to have lied.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: {rival} sat in that chair an hour ago and said yes before I'd finished the question. I'm not saying it to needle you. It's just what I'll remember.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: {name}. I'm three doors down and I've been meaning to knock for a fortnight. The fortnight got away from me.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Hello. {name}, {riding}. I don't actually need anything, which I'm told makes me unusual.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: {name}. I don't do the Wednesday dinners and I don't do the lobby gossip. I do like to know who my neighbours are.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: {name}. I've just been told my office is being moved to make room for someone's chief of staff. Sorry. You're not who I'm angry at.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I'm {name}. The whip's office sent me a form letter about attendance in my first week. I thought I'd come and see who signs them.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I'm {name}, from {riding}. Did you get the binder? Nobody told me there was a binder, and apparently there's a binder.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: {name}, new member for {riding}. I was told to come and present myself. I wasn't told what happens after that.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I'm on the {interest} committee, by some accident of scheduling. If you ever need something moved there, ask me before you ask the clerk.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Here's what I've learnt in a month: the staff know everything and the members know nothing. Make friends with the staff.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I'll tell you what I tell everyone. I'm loyal until it costs {riding}. Then I'm {riding}'s. Best you know that now.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Three members from {riding} have come through here before me. Two of them forgot where it was. I'd like to be the one who didn't.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: You know what nobody tells you? The whip's office has your schedule before you do. I found out about my own committee from a reporter.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Three weeks in and I've already been told to stop asking questions in caucus. Apparently that's not what caucus is for.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Can I ask you something? Does anyone actually read the briefing notes, or is everyone pretending, like I am?

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I keep waiting for someone to find out I don't know what I'm doing. Is that normal, or should I be more worried?

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Right, that's the introductions done. Next time we'll skip them and go straight to the complaining.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Come to the {clique} table at lunch sometime. They're loud, but they share.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: That'll do for a first conversation. We'll see what the second one's like.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I don't make friends quickly here. I do make them properly. Give it time.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Thanks for letting me vent. You're the first person today who didn't look at their phone while I did it.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Anyway. I've said more than I meant to. If any of it reaches the whip, I'll know it was you or the walls.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: That helped. Honestly. Can we do it again when I've actually read the binder?

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I'll stop taking up your evening. If you hear my name in the lobby, I'd be grateful to know what they said.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: You're the one who voted against the line. I wanted to see what that looks like up close. Tired, mostly.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: They said to congratulate you on the new office before asking for anything. So: congratulations. I'll come back for the asking.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: People say {playerRiding} would elect you for life. I'd settle for one more term. How do you do it?

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I'll be two minutes. Three if you offer me a drink, so don't.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: You've got the whip's ear now, or you are the whip's ear, I lose track. Either way, I need it for a minute.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I don't ask lightly, and I'll say up front that I'll remember either answer.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: You can say no. I'd rather you said it tonight than let me find out on Thursday.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: The whip's office said no before I'd finished the sentence. I'm hoping you'll at least let me finish it.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I've had the runaround from three offices today. You're the fourth. Make me feel better about the number.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Have you got a minute? Say yes. I've already rehearsed this in the corridor.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: There's a delegation from {riding} here on Thursday and I'm double-booked. Walk them through the lobby for me. Twenty minutes they'll talk about for years.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I'm putting a question on {interest} on the order paper. It needs a seconder from outside {riding}, and one who won't be talked out of it.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: There's a photo on {interest} next week and my name's been left off the list. I want you to ask why, because when I ask, nothing happens.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: My pair fell through for Friday and the whip's office shrugged. I need to be in {riding} for a funeral. Find me a pair, or be one.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: The paper at home is running a piece on how I've done nothing on {interest}. One line from you in the House gives me something to send them.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I need a letter. Just a letter, to the minister, with your name beside mine. It's about {riding}, and it costs you nothing but ink.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: So? I'll take a nod. I've seen whole careers built on a nod.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: There it is. I don't like asking, so I won't ask twice.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: You've heard it. I'll leave you to decide what it's worth to you.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Well? I'd like one person in this building to say yes to me today, and it would be convenient if it were you.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Don't tell me you'll think about it. I've been thought about by better people than you, and nothing came of it.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: If it's no, say it kindly. I've had a week.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I know it's a lot to walk in with. I wouldn't be here if I had anywhere else to go.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Now that you've got a window, I'm hoping the office comes with a longer reach. Here's my problem.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I hear things are rough in {playerRiding}. I'll be quick, then. You've got enough on your plate.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: You've voted the line every time, which means the whip owes you. I'm hoping some of that can rub off on me.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: This isn't a shouting match. I just think you should hear it from me before you hear a version of it from someone else.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I'm here as a friend, which is why I'm here at all. Most people would have just stopped speaking to you.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I'll keep this short. Something you did landed on me, and I'd like to know whether you meant it to.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I've been turning something over for a week. I'd rather say it than keep turning it.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Sit down. No, I'll stand. I want to be able to leave when I've said this.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I defended you in caucus last month. I'd like to know why I bothered.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Your office pulled my pair with four hours' notice. I missed my daughter's recital for a vote we won by thirty.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I don't know how to say this without it sounding like an accusation, so I'm going to say it and you can tell me if I'm wrong.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Please don't take this the wrong way. I've been dreading this conversation since Tuesday.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: You got the credit for the {interest} announcement. Half that work was mine, and the paper in {riding} ran it under your name.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: You were asked about {riding} on the radio and said you didn't know the file. I'd briefed you on it twice.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: You took a meeting with my riding association without telling me. Whatever you said, they came away thinking I'm on the way out.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Your office asked the clerk to move my committee slot and didn't think to mention it. I found the change in the order paper.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: You stood up in caucus and used my riding as the example of 'where we're weak'. In front of {other}. In front of everyone.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: You promised me a word with the minister. The minister tells me the word was about you.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: People are saying I've gone soft on the leadership, and the only person I ever said that to was you.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: {other} told me you'd said I wasn't ready for committee. If you think that, I'd rather hear it from you than from {other}.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: That's all. I'm not keeping score. But I'd like you to know I noticed.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Look, we're going to be in rooms together for years. Let's not make this one of the things we remember.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I'll leave it there. You know what I think now, and I'll know what you think by what you do.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: An apology would have been nice. I'll settle for it not happening again.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Fix it. I don't much care how. And if I hear my name in your mouth in caucus again, we'll be having this conversation in front of the whip.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I'm done. Make it right or don't. Either way, I vote my own count from now on, not yours.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I just want to be able to sit next to you at caucus without wondering. Is that something you can give me?

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Tell me we're all right. And then show me, because I've been told things before.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I know the leader's office is on your back. That's no excuse for what landed on mine.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Pour yourself something. I've got a story and it's a good one.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I've been saving this all afternoon. You're the first person I've told, which should tell you something.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: This stays in this room. I mean it. I've already told two people and that's one too many.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I'm telling the whip's office this because I'd rather you heard it from me than from your board.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I'm so angry I could spit. Guess who's been talking to the other side's whip.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Do you want to know why your committee slot moved? Because I know, and it'll make you furious.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Can I ask you something quietly? Have you heard anything about a shuffle?

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I don't know whether this is nothing or everything. Tell me which.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: {other} went into the leader's office at four and came out at six with a face like a wedding. Something's been promised.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: The whip's office has started asking who has lunch with whom. {other} was asked about you, apparently. Nicely, they said.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: The committee chairs for the spring are already decided. I've seen the list. {clique} did well out of it. You didn't.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: {other} has been quietly asking members what they'd want for a nay on the next big one. Somebody's counting who isn't the whip.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: {other} has been telling the gallery that half the cohort are 'rural rubes who'll vote how they're told'. Off the record, of course. Everything is.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: The money for {otherRiding} came through in a week. Mine's been in the queue since the spring. Guess whose cousin works in the minister's office.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Someone's been through the pairing book. The Clerk's office noticed. If it's the other side, fine. If it's ours, somebody's being set up.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I heard my name on the list for a boundary review. If they carve up {riding}, I'm finished, and so is {other}.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Right, I've unburdened myself. Use it wisely, or at least amusingly.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: That's all I've got. If you hear the next chapter before I do, I expect a knock.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Don't act on it yet. The ones who move first on a rumour are usually the ones it was meant for.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I've told you because you'd have heard a worse version by Friday. Now you've got the right one.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I'd love to say something in caucus. I won't, because I'd like to keep my committee seat. But somebody should.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Anyway. Now you know why I'm in a mood. Pass it on or don't. I'm past caring who knows.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: If it turns out to be nothing, forget I said anything. If it isn't, remember I said it first.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Do you think I should go to the whip? Don't answer that. I already know what you'd say.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Your friend {rival} has been busy. You'll want to be sitting down for this.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Since you crossed the whip, people have started telling me things about you. I thought you'd want to know what.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Word is the leader's office has a file with your name on it. I'm telling you because nobody told me when it was mine.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I've watched you in caucus. You ask the question everyone else is thinking. I'm here to ask you one back, about {bill}.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Relax, I'm not the whip's office. If anything I'm the opposite. It's about {bill}.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Before I say anything, I need to know you won't go straight down the hall when I leave. It's about {bill}.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I'll say this once and you can decide whether you heard it. There's a group forming on {bill}.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I know which office you sit in now. That's why I'm here. You can carry this down the hall, or you can hear it. It's about {bill}.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: They want us to vote for {bill} and smile for the photo. I'm done smiling.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I've had it. I spent the morning reading {bill} and the afternoon being told what I think of it.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I need to be careful how I say this. There are people who'd like {bill} to fail, and I'm one of them, and I can't be the only one.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Can I close the door? I shouldn't be here, and I'd rather nobody saw me not being here.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: It's not a revolt, it's arithmetic. Eight of us abstain, the margin on {bill} is gone, and suddenly the minister wants to talk amendments.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: We've got a lawyer drafting the amendment on {interest} tonight. All we need is enough names that the whip can't ignore it.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Nobody's name goes on paper. We each tell the whip we're 'reflecting' until the morning of the vote. Then we see who meant it.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I've got four who'll go if there are six. I've got six if there are eight. You'd be the sixth.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: You count the room. You know better than anyone how many of us are soft on {bill}. I'm asking you to let the count be honest.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: {bill} closes the office in {riding} that half my casework goes through. They didn't ask. They never ask. So I'm not asking either.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: The whip says rebels don't get committee chairs. I said members who vote for {bill} don't get re-elected in {riding}. We're at an impasse.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: If this gets out before the vote, they'll pick us off one by one. That's what happened last time. I was there.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I've been counting on a napkin for a week. The number keeps changing, and I keep hoping it's you who changes it.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: So. In or out? No hard feelings either way. Well, some, but I'll get over it.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Sleep on it, but not for long. {bill} won't wait and neither will the whip.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I'm going to leave now, and tomorrow I'll find out whether I should have come. Goodnight.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: If you're in, say nothing to anyone and be in your seat with your hands in your lap. If you're out, say nothing to anyone. That's all I ask.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: You'll have to decide what you are first. I'll know from the board.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Decide. I've got three more doors to knock on and the night's not getting younger.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I didn't come for a maybe. If you're with {riding} and {playerRiding}, stand with them. If you're with the whip, say so and I'll leave.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Please think about it. And please don't tell them I was here. Even if it's no.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: I'll go before someone sees the light under the door. If you hear nothing from me, I lost my nerve. If you hear from me, I didn't.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: You've done it once. That's why I'm in your office and not someone else's.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: You've never voted against the line, which means that if you did, they'd notice. That's the point.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Sit me anywhere. I've been expecting this since the order paper came out.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Let's save us both an hour. Tell me what you need, and I'll tell you what it costs.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: What's the count on {bill} tonight? The real one, not the one for {leader}.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: You know what {bill} does to {playerRiding}. You've read the same briefing I have.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Is this going to take long? I've got a riding call at nine and they don't like waiting.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I know why I'm here. I'll make it easy on both of us.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'm not trying to make your week harder. I know how many of these chairs you've filled tonight.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Here's what I'd need to stand up on {bill}: something I can put in a newsletter with a straight face.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Tell me who else is wobbling. I'd like to know whose company I'm in.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: You can list the committees I won't get. I'll list the doors in {playerRiding} I won't be able to knock on.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Could we pick this up after caucus? I'd like to hear what the room thinks first.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: You've made the case. I won't pretend I like it, but I heard it.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: You'll have my answer before the bells, and you'll have it in person. That's all I can promise tonight.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Yea, on one condition: the office returns the call when {playerRiding} rings. That's the price.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Give me the night. I'll read the amendments once more and tell you first thing.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Write me down as against. I'd rather be a problem on your board than a stranger at home.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Leaning yea. Ask me again tomorrow and it might be firmer.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Mark me firm. I'll be in my seat when the Speaker calls it.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Door's open, chair's clean. That's the best offer you'll get on this floor.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Nice to meet you. Who do you sit with, and who do you vote with?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Sit. Tell me what the first weeks have been like for you.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Good. I keep a list of who came by in the first month. You're on the right side of it.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Is it just me, or does every corridor in this building look the same?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: You beat me to it. I kept meaning to introduce myself and kept losing the afternoon.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: What do you miss most? For me it's walking to the shop without needing a position on everything.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: What's the one thing you'd walk out of caucus over? Everyone has one.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Say more. I'd rather hear it from you than the version going round the lobby.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'll be honest, I'm sizing you up. Everyone in this building does it. I'm just saying so.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Let's save the big questions for a night when neither of us has a committee at eight.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'll admit I'd heard things about you. I'm glad I waited to make up my own mind.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: We should do this properly some week. Dinner, away from the Hill, nobody taking notes.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: If something's coming that touches {riding} and {playerRiding} both, call me first. I'll do the same.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'll remember that. And I'll remember you came by before you needed anything.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Good. Just know I don't forget a favour, and I don't forget the other thing either.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Let's see how we both survive the first session. Then we'll talk about alliances.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: You've thought about this more than I have. I'll take my cue from you for a while.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Pull up the chair. The good one, not the one with the wobble.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Tell me what you want and what you think it's worth.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: All right. What's the problem underneath the ask?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Favours in this building are loans. I'll want to know when you're good for it.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: If it involves the whip's office, I'd rather not. If it doesn't, go on.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: You've had my back before. Ask.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I can hear what this means to you. Let's see if we can get there.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I can do that. The question is what you'd do for {playerRiding} when it's my turn.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Who else have you asked, and what did they say? I'd like to know what I'm walking into.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: That's not small. Don't call it small. If I do this, it goes in my book under your name.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: That's a bigger ask than you made it sound. Let me think about how it would look.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Fine. I'd be a hypocrite to refuse. I've asked for worse.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: You've got it. And {riding} should know who went to bat for them. Tell them.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Yes, in exchange for a seconder when I need one. Shake on it.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Give me a day to see what's already on my plate. You'll have a straight answer by then.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'll help. But I'll remember the weight of it, and so should you.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'll try. Don't tell anyone it's done until it is.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Done. Don't thank me. Do the same for the next one who asks you.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Shut the door and say it. I'd rather hear it here than read it in a note.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Right. Tell me exactly what happened, in order.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'm listening. Start wherever it starts.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Before you start: I'm hearing the complaint, not the threat. Leave the threat outside.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Can this wait till after the vote? I'm not sure either of us is at our best tonight.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: If you've come all this way, I probably deserve it. Go ahead.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I can see why you're angry. I would be. Let me tell you what happened, and you decide if it's enough.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Here's what I can do about it, tonight. Tell me if it's enough or if you need more.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: What's the version of this that's going round? I need to know what you've heard, not just what happened.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: You've got your facts half right. The other half makes you look worse than me, so let's be careful here.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: There's more to it than that. I'm not sure tonight's the night to get into all of it.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: You're right, and I'm sorry. I should have come to you first instead of letting you find out sideways.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'd like to fix this, and I'd like us to be able to laugh about it by the spring. Let me start on the first part.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'll say something in caucus on Wednesday, with your name in it. That's what you came for, isn't it?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Is there anything else? I'd rather hear all of it tonight than have it come back in pieces.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'll make it right. Then we're even, and I'll expect the same consideration next time it's you.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Let's both sleep on it. I'm not sure either of us will remember this the same way next week.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Consider it fixed. Tell me the day after if it isn't.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Sit down, close the door. You've got that look.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Go on. Who, and what did they do?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Start from the beginning. Who told you?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: If this touches the count, I need to know before the whip does. Agreed?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Is this real, or lobby talk? I've been burnt by lobby talk.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I've been buried in committee all week. Tell me what I've missed.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: That's a lot to carry. You did right to say it out loud.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Does the whip know? And if not, who's going to tell them?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: And what do you think it means? You know these people better than I do.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: If {other} is doing that, somebody needs to stop it before it costs us a vote.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: People say things in the lobby they'd never say in caucus. I'd wait to see it in writing.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I believe you. I've seen enough of {other} to know it fits.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Thanks for coming to me. I know you didn't have to.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: If you hear more, I want it the same hour. I'll do the same for you.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'll listen out. If I hear your name, you'll hear from me first.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'll sit on it for now. But if it starts moving, I'm moving with it, and I'd like you beside me.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Most of this building's rumours die by Friday. Let's see if this one does.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: It stays in this room. I won't even tell my staff.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: You're safe here. Say what you came to say.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: How many, and who's counting?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'll hear you out. I've read {bill}. I know what's in it.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Careful. There are doors in this corridor that report to the whip. You've chosen mine. Why?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I don't know that I've got a view on {bill} yet. Committee hasn't reported.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Thank God. I thought I was the only one who'd actually read it.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I know what {bill} does to places like {riding}. I'm not going to pretend otherwise.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Say the whip offers you an amendment tomorrow. Do you take it, or is this about more than {bill}?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Who's firm and who's hoping? There's a difference, and it's the whole game.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: If you've miscounted, the ones who go down are the ones with the thinnest margins. That's you, and that's me.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'd want to hear from {playerRiding} before I move. They're the ones who'll live with it.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Someone has to say it in a way they can't ignore. I've been waiting for someone to organise it.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Whatever I do, nobody will hear from me that you were in this room.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'll abstain. That's as far as I go without an amendment on the table.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Come back when you've got the number. I'll tell you then.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Drop it. You haven't got the votes, and the whip has a longer memory than you do.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Ask me the morning of the vote. I'll know by then what I can live with.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'm in. For {playerRiding}, and because somebody has to be.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: {name}, {riding}. All day I've been told where to sit and when to clap. I wanted five minutes with someone who isn't telling me anything.

lines.speaker: mp
lines.text: Sit down and look bored. If anyone walks past, we're talking about the committee schedule.

lines.speaker: whip
lines.text: Good, you came yourself. Half of them send a staffer with an excuse. {bill} is close, and I'm asking the people I trust first.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: Good. I'll hold you to that, and you can hold me to mine.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: Shake on it, then. I don't put these things in writing, and I'd advise you not to either.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: That's a fair trade. Rarer than you'd think in this building.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: Done. If anyone asks, we talked about the weather in {riding}.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: I'll remember this. Around here that's usually a threat. Tonight it isn't.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: We're agreed. I knew we'd get somewhere if we kept the door shut.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: All right. I'll be watching to see that you keep your end.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: Fine. It doesn't make us friends, but it's a start.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: Thank you. I didn't know who else to ask, if I'm honest.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: Then we're agreed on {bill}. Keep your head down until the bells, and tell the whip's office nothing.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: That's one more for {bill}. When the count comes out wrong, they won't know where to look.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: I owe you, and I won't forget which one.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: You've made my week. Don't let me forget I said that.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: Let's call it settled. I'd rather have you inside the tent than writing to the papers about it.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: We're done here. Don't come looking for me when you need a vote.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: I didn't climb four flights of stairs for that.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: Thank you for your time, such as it was.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: I'll find someone who can make a real offer.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: That's insulting, and I'll be telling people exactly how insulting.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: I thought you were one of the sensible ones. My mistake.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: Forget I came by. And forget what I said about {bill}.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: No? Then I'll ask someone who remembers what a favour is.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: Your loss. That offer won't be on the table tomorrow.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: Suit yourself. I thought we were close.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: Walking away is a position too, I suppose. Not a good one.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: I'll take the long way back to my office. Gives me time to think about who else to ask.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: Another time, then.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: I'll take that as a no. Politely delivered, at least.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: Think it over. The door's open until it isn't.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: Sleep on it. The vote on {bill} won't wait for you to wake up.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: Never mind. I'll ask someone else, and they'll ask why you didn't help.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: Right. I'll stop taking up your evening.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: Good to talk properly. That doesn't happen much in this place.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: I'll let you get on. Your evening's no freer than mine.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: Don't be a stranger. The ones who hide in their offices don't last.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: Glad we did this. Find me in the lobby if you're ever lost.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: Right, I've kept you long enough. Welcome to the madhouse.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: Nice to put a face to the seat number.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: You didn't hear any of that from me.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: Keep it to yourself for a day or two. After that it'll be everywhere anyway.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: Off you go. And {playerFirst}: sleep. Nobody makes a good call in here on four hours.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: Mind what I said. I won't say it twice, because I won't need to.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: My door's open. Use it before things go wrong, not after.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: I've said my piece. Whether you heard it is your business.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: Fine. We'll see if anything changes.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: I came to clear the air. It's no clearer.

partings.speaker: whip
partings.text: Good. I'll mark you down as firm. Don't make me rub it out.

partings.speaker: whip
partings.text: That's what I needed to hear. The leader will hear it too.

partings.speaker: whip
partings.text: Thank you. You'd be amazed how few of these end with a handshake.

partings.speaker: whip
partings.text: Done. Go home, get some sleep, and be in your seat when the bells go on {bill}.

partings.speaker: whip
partings.text: Thank God. One less name on my list of worries.

partings.speaker: whip
partings.text: Fine. We're square for now. Keep it that way.

partings.speaker: whip
partings.text: I see. I'll write that down, and so will the leader's office.

partings.speaker: whip
partings.text: Then I hope {playerRiding} is worth it, because it may be all you'll have.

partings.speaker: whip
partings.text: Disappointing. Close the door on your way out.

partings.speaker: whip
partings.text: Vote with your conscience, then. Your conscience doesn't draw up the committee lists.

partings.speaker: whip
partings.text: You know how close this count is. I'll pretend you didn't just do that.

partings.speaker: whip
partings.text: I respect it. I don't like it, but I respect it. Don't make a habit of it.

partings.speaker: whip
partings.text: That's not a trade, that's a ransom. The offer was the offer.

partings.speaker: whip
partings.text: No. I've got thirty of you to keep, and I can't pay every one of them that.

partings.speaker: whip
partings.text: You've overplayed it. Come back when you've remembered whose office this is.

partings.speaker: whip
partings.text: I'll find the vote somewhere cheaper. There's always somewhere cheaper.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: That's done, then. I'll tell my staff to stop drafting the letter they were going to send you.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: We'll both deny this happened, which is how you know it was a good deal.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: You've no idea how much lighter that makes the walk back.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: Lovely. Secrets for favours. That's how the building was built.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: A deal in the first month. They warned me about you. They were right, in a good way.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: I came in here as a colleague. I'm leaving as a lesson.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: I'd heard you were careful. I hadn't heard you were cheap.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: I shouldn't have come. I knew I shouldn't have come.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: Right. Then we'll let the room decide who was wronged.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: Go on, then. The door was always the easiest thing in this building to find.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: I'll remember this when you're the one knocking.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: Oh. I thought we were nearly there.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: That's a shame. I thought we were getting somewhere. Maybe next time.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: Fair enough. Not every conversation has to end in a handshake.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: All right. I'll think of something else. I always do, eventually.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: No harm done. We'll talk again when the arithmetic's different.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: So nothing changes. Noted.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: Good. Go and eat something. You look like the vending machine's been feeding you.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: Same time next crisis.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: I've said more than I meant to. Forget half of it.

partings.speaker: mp
partings.text: That'll do. I've learnt what I came to learn.

partings.speaker: whip
partings.text: Good. Now go and look confident in the lobby. Half this job is looking confident in the lobby.

partings.speaker: whip
partings.text: In ink, then. Don't make me find the rubber.

partings.speaker: whip
partings.text: I knew I could count on you. I like being right. It's rarer than you'd think.

partings.speaker: whip
partings.text: Fine. I'll find the vote somewhere. I always do. But I'll remember where I didn't find it.

partings.speaker: whip
partings.text: Out. And don't expect the office to pick up when {playerRiding} rings.

partings.speaker: whip
partings.text: Noted. That's a small word with a long life in this building.

partings.speaker: whip
partings.text: I'm the whip, not the Treasury. The answer's no.

partings.speaker: whip
partings.text: Ask me for something I've actually got and we'll talk. That isn't one of them.

partings.speaker: whip
partings.text: I can't. I'd like to, and I can't, and you've just made my night longer.
